title: Mate with two bishops

D0.outcome: Explains the two-bishop mate: drive the king to the edge and into a corner, bring the king to the sixth rank, and use a waiting bishop move.

D1.outcome: Mates with two bishops against a bare king in a given position within 25 moves.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled positions, mates without stalemating and without losing a bishop, choosing the waiting move correctly.

D3.outcome: Verifies the move count against the tablebase and finds the quickest method.

misconceptions: Place the bishops anywhere; they will drive the king.
conditions: Both bishops restrict the king; the king must be driven to the edge and into a corner, and the attacker's king reaches the sixth rank; White must mark time with a bishop move.
contrasts: Placing the bishops without a plan, or forgetting to bring the king up.
Bishops on the same colour (which cannot mate).
